atoms.title: The Lawmaking Process: A Minimum Wage Bill

atoms.text:
Step 1: Introducing a bill
A member of Congress introduces a bill that proposes to raise the minimum wage to $15/hour.
atoms.sound: Step 1, Introducing a bill. A member of Congress introduces a bill that proposes to raise the minimum wage to 15 dollars an hour.

atoms.a: Who can propose the bill in Congress?

atoms.text:
Step 2: Committee review
The bill goes to a committee that specializes in the topic, which holds hearings with workers and economists and amends the bill.
atoms.sound: Step 2, Committee review. The bill goes to a committee that specializes in the topic, which holds hearings with workers and economists and amends the bill.

atoms.a: In the case of the minimum wage bill, which committee is suitable to hold the hearings?
b: ++the House Committee on Education and Labor
the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee

atoms.text:
Step 3: Floor vote
The full House or Senate debates the bill and votes. If it passes, it goes to the other chamber, which repeats steps 2–3.
atoms.sound: Step 3, Floor vote. The full House or Senate debates the bill and votes. If it passes, it goes to the other chamber, which repeats steps 2 to 3.

atoms.a: The House passes the bill. Which chamber discusses and votes next?

atoms.text:
Step 4: Reconciliation
The House and Senate versions differ on how fast wages increase, so a conference committee agrees on a compromise.
atoms.sound: Step 4, Reconciliation. The House and Senate versions differ on how fast wages increase, so a conference committee agrees on a compromise.

atoms.a: Why may the two chamber's versions differ?
b: ++Each chamber holds their own hearing and can amend the proposed bill.
Two separate bills were originally proposed.
Only one of the chambers reviewed the bill.

atoms.text:
Step 5: President’s decision
The President can sign the bill into law, veto it, or take no action. Congress can override a veto with a two-thirds vote in both the House and Senate.
However, if the President does not sign off on a bill and it remains unsigned when Congress is no longer in session, the bill will be vetoed by default. This action is called a pocket veto, and cannot be overridden by Congress.
atoms.sound: Step 5, President’s decision. The President can sign the bill into law, veto it, or take no action. Congress can override a veto with a two-thirds vote in both the House and Senate. However, if the President does not sign off on a bill and it remains unsigned when Congress is no longer in session, the bill will be vetoed by default. This action is called a pocket veto, and cannot be overridden by Congress.

atoms.a: The president refuses to approve the minimum wage bill (veto). How could it still become law?
b: ++Congress overrides the veto with a ⅔ vote in both chambers.
It cannot because this is a pocket veto.
Half of Congress overrides the veto.

atoms.text: Congress has overridden the President's veto by a two-third majority and the minimum wage bill is signed into law – raising the minimum wage to $15/hour.
